title: First Steps
subtitle: Find your way around the keyboard

lessons.title: Meet middle C
body: The black keys come in groups of two and three. Find the group of two black keys closest to the middle of your piano.
The white key just to the left of that group is middle C. Every note you will learn is measured from here.
Rest your right thumb on middle C and play it every time a note reaches the line.

lessons.title: Five fingers, five notes
body: Place your right-hand fingers on C, D, E, F and G: thumb on C, pinky on G. This is the C position.
Keep your fingers curved, as if you were holding a small ball. Each finger plays only its own key.

lessons.title: Your left hand
body: Your left hand mirrors your right. Place your pinky on the C below middle C and your thumb on G.
Left-hand notes are written on the bass staff, the lower of the two staves.

lessons.title: Hands together
body: Now combine both hands. The left hand holds long notes while the right hand moves.
Practise each hand alone first, then put them together. Wait mode will hold the music until you play the right notes.

lessons.title: Treble clef landmarks
body: The treble clef curls around the second line from the bottom. That line is G above middle C.
Middle C sits on its own short line just below the treble staff. The C one octave higher is in the third space.

lessons.title: Bass clef landmarks
body: The two dots of the bass clef surround the fourth line. That line is F below middle C.
The C below middle C is in the second space of the bass staff.

lessons.title: Steps and skips
body: A step moves from a line to the next space, or from a space to the next line. A skip jumps over one note: line to line, or space to space.
Watch the shape of the notes and you will know where your hand is going before you read every name.

lessons.title: The C major triad
body: A triad is three notes stacked in skips. C major is C, E and G. Play them with your thumb, middle finger and pinky.
Press all three keys at the same moment. In wait mode the music moves on once every note of the chord is down.

lessons.title: I – IV – V – I
body: Most popular songs are built on three chords: the I, IV and V of the key. In C major they are C, F and G.
Move your hand as little as possible: keep the shared notes where they are and slide only the fingers that must move.

lessons.title: Broken chords
body: A broken chord plays the notes of a chord one after another. It is the most common left-hand accompaniment.
Keep your left hand still above the chord, and let your fingers do the moving.
